questions.stem:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I | List-II
A. Planck's constant | I. $ML^{2}T^{-2}$
B. Stopping potential | II. $T^{-1}$
C. Work function | III. $ML^{2}T^{-1}$
D. Threshold frequency | IV. $ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-1}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$E = h\nu \Rightarrow [h] = \frac{[E]}{[\nu]} = \frac{ML^{2}T^{-2}}{T^{-1}} = ML^{2}T^{-1} \rightarrow \text{III}$
$U = qV \Rightarrow [V] = \frac{[U]}{[q]} = \frac{ML^{2}T^{-2}}{AT} = ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-1} \rightarrow \text{IV}$
$K_{max} = h\nu - \phi \Rightarrow [\phi] = [K_{max}] = ML^{2}T^{-2} \rightarrow \text{I}$
[Threshold frequency] = [frequency] = $T^{-1} \rightarrow \text{II}$

questions.stem: Two cars A and B are moving in the same direction along a straight line with speeds 100 km/h and 80 km/h, respectively such that car A is moving ahead of car B. A person in car B throws a stone with a speed v so that it hits the car A with a speed of 5 m/s. The value of v is ________ km/h.
questions.solution:
Let velocity of stone relative to ground = $v_{0}$
Then $v_{0} - 80 = v$ .........(1)
Velocity of stone wrt A = $v_{0} - 100 = 5 \times \frac{36}{10}$
$v_{0} = 118$ km/hr
(1) $\rightarrow 118 - 80 = v = 38$ km/hr $\rightarrow$ (3)

questions.stem: At t = 0, a body of mass 100 g starts moving under the influence of a force $(5\hat{i} + 10\hat{j})\ \mathrm{N}$. After 2 s its position is $(2x\hat{i} + 5y\hat{j})\ \mathrm{m}$. The ratio x : y is ________ .

If x and y coordinates of a projectile as a function of time (t) are given as 24t and $43.6t - 4.9t^{2}$, respectively, then the angle (in degrees) made by the projectile with horizontal when t = 2 s is ______ .
questions.solution:
$x = 24t \Rightarrow v_{x} = 24$
$y = 43.6t - 4.9t^{2}$
$\Rightarrow v_{y} = 43.6 - 4.9 \times 2 \times t = 24$ (at t = 2s)
$\Rightarrow \tan\theta = \frac{v_{y}}{v_{x}} = \frac{24}{24} = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = 45^\circ$

questions.stem: The height in terms of radius of the earth (R), at which the acceleration due to gravity becomes $\frac{g}{9}$, where g is acceleration due to gravity on earth's surface, is _________ .
questions.solution:
$\frac{GM}{r^{2}} = \frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{GM}{R^{2}} \Rightarrow r = 3R$
$h = r - R = 2R$

questions.stem: A metal string A is suspended from a rigid support and its free end is attached to a block of mass M. Second block having mass 2 M is suspended at the bottom of the first block using a string B. The area of cross sections of strings A and B are same. The ratio of lengths of strings of A to B is 2 and the ratio of their Young's moduli $(Y_{A}/Y_{B})$ is 0.5 . The ratio of elongations in A to B is ___________ .
questions.solution:
(Figure: string A of length $2l$, Young's modulus Y, area A, elongation $\Delta l_{1}$, tension $T_{1}$, holding block M; string B of length $l$, Young's modulus 2Y, area A, elongation $\Delta l_{2}$, tension $T_{2}$, holding block 2M)
$T_{1} = 3mg, \quad T_{2} = 2mg$
For B
$\frac{2Mg/A}{\Delta l_{2}/l} = 2Y$ .........(1)
For A
$\frac{3Mg/A}{\Delta l_{1}/2l} = y$ .........(2)
(1) / (2) : $\frac{\Delta l_{1}}{\Delta l_{2}} = 6$

questions.stem: A water spray gun is attached to a hose of cross sectional area $30\ \mathrm{cm^{2}}$. The gun comprises of 10 perforations each of cross sectional area of $15\ \mathrm{mm^{2}}$. If the water flows in the hose with the speed of $50\ \mathrm{cm/s}$, calculate the speed at which the water flows out from each perforation. (Neglect any edge effects)
questions.solution:
$A_{1}v_{1} = A_{2}v_{2}$
$30 \times 50 = (15 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}}) \times 10 \times v \Rightarrow v = 1000$ cm/s
$v = 10$ m/s

Reason R: The r.m.s. speed of $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2}$ molecules are same at same temperature.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explantion of A

questions.stem:
The temperature of a metal strip having coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$ is increased from $T_{1}$ to $T_{2}$ resulting in increase of its length by $\Delta L_{1}$. The temperature is further increased from $T_{2}$ to $T_{3}$ such that the increase in its length is $\Delta L_{2}$.
Given $T_{3} + T_{1} = 2T_{2}$ and $T_{2} - T_{1} = \Delta T$, the value of $\Delta L_{2}$ is
questions.solution:
(Figure: strip at $T_{1}$ with length $L_{0}$ $\xrightarrow{\Delta T\uparrow,\ \Delta L_{1}\uparrow}$ strip at $T_{2}$ with length $L_{0}(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$ $\xrightarrow{\Delta T\uparrow,\ \Delta L_{2}\uparrow}$ strip at $T_{3}$)
$T_{3} + T_{1} = 2T_{2} = T_{2} - T_{1} = T_{3} - T_{2} = \Delta T$
$\Delta L_{1} = L_{0}\alpha\Delta T$
$\Delta L_{2} = L_{0}(1 + \alpha\Delta T) \cdot \alpha\Delta T$
$= (L_{0}\alpha\Delta T)(1 + \alpha\Delta T) = \Delta L_{1}(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$

questions.stem:
A uniform disc of radius R and mass M is free to oscillate about the axis A as shown in the figure. For small oscillations the time period is _________ .
( g is acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{I}{Mgl}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\frac{5}{4}MR^{2}}{MgR}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{5R}{4g}}$

questions.stem: A rigid dipole undergoes a simple harmonic motion about its centre in the presence of an electric field $\vec{E}_{1} = E_{0}\hat{x}$. If another electric field $\vec{E}_{2} = 2E_{0}(\hat{y} + \hat{z})$ is introduced to the system, what will be the percentage change in the frequency of the oscillation (approximate)?
questions.solution:
$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{I}{pE}} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f \propto \sqrt{E}$
$f_{1} \propto \sqrt{E_{0}}$
$\vec{E} = E_{0}\hat{x} + 2E_{0}\hat{y} + 2E_{0}\hat{z}$
$\Rightarrow |\vec{E}| = 3E_{0}$
$f_{2} \propto \sqrt{3E_{0}}$
$\%\,\text{change} = \frac{f_{2} - f_{1}}{f_{1}} \times 100 = \left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{1}\right) \times 100 = 73\%$

questions.stem:
A solenoid has a core made of material with relative permeability 400 . The magnetic field produced in the interior of solenoid is 1.0 T . The magnetic intensity in SI units is $\alpha \times 10^{5}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________ .
(Free space permeability $\mu_{0} = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ SI units.)
questions.solution:
$B = \mu H \Rightarrow H = \frac{B}{\mu} = \frac{1}{400 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-7}} = \frac{10^{5}}{16\pi} = \alpha \times 10^{5}$
$\alpha = \frac{1}{16\pi}$

questions.stem: A magnetic field vector in an electromagnetic wave is represented by $\vec{B} = B_{0}\sin\left(2\pi\nu t - \frac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right)\hat{j}$. Its associated electric field vector is ________ .
questions.solution:
(Figure: axes x, y, z with $\vec{B}$ along y, wave velocity c along x, and $\vec{E}$ shown)
$E_{0} = cB_{0}$
$= \nu\lambda B_{0}$
$\vec{E} = \vec{B} \times \vec{C}$
$\vec{E}$ should ln along $-\hat{k}$ (as per right hand rule)
$\vec{E} = -\nu\lambda B_{0}\sin\left(2\pi\nu t - \frac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right)\hat{k}$

questions.stem: A convex lens is made from glass material having refractive index of 1.4 with same radius of curvature on both sides. The ratio of its focal length and radius of curvature is _________ .

An unpolarized light of certain intensity passes through a combination of two polarizers whose transmission axes are at $30^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, respectively, with respect to the horizontal axis. A third polarizer with its transmission axis at $60^\circ$ with the horizontal axis is placed between the two existing polarizers. The ratio of the output intensities with and without the third polarizer is __________ .
questions.solution:
Without third polarizer:
$I_{1} = \frac{I_{0}}{2} \times \cos^{2}60^\circ$
With third polarizer:
$I_{2} = \frac{I_{0}}{2} \times \cos^{2}30^\circ \times \cos^{2}30^\circ$
$\frac{I_{2}}{I_{1}} = \frac{9}{4}$

questions.stem:
In Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment, only a few alpha particles rebound back because
A. The size of gold nucleus is very small as compared to the size of gold atom.
B. Alpha particle and gold nucleus have equal charge.
C. The impact parameter is minimum for a few alpha particles.
D. A few alpha particles have very high kinetic energy.
E. Only a few alpha particles undergo head-on collision with the nuclei.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Only a few $\alpha$-particles rebound back, because :
$\rightarrow$ Size of sold nucleus is very small
$\rightarrow$ Impact parameter is very small for very few $\alpha$-particles
$\rightarrow$ Head on collision occurs for very few $\alpha$-particles

questions.stem: The de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron accelerated through a potential difference V is $\lambda_{e}$ and the de Broglie wavelength associated with a proton accelerated through the same potential difference is $\lambda_{p}$. If their corresponding masses are $m_{e}$ and $m_{p}$, respectively, then the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths $\left(\frac{\lambda_{e}}{\lambda_{p}}\right)$ is ________ .
questions.solution:
$\lambda_{e} = \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{2m_{e}eV}}, \quad \lambda_{p} = \frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{2m_{p}eV}}$
$\frac{\lambda_{e}}{\lambda_{p}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{p}}{m_{e}}}$

questions.stem: A diode has Zener voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.5 W , then the minimum resistance to be used in series with this diode for safety when it is connected to a 25 V power supply is ____________ $\Omega$.
questions.solution:
(Figure: 25 V supply in series with resistor R and the Zener diode (10 V); current I)
For diode :
$P = VI$
$0.5 = 10 \times I$
$\Rightarrow I = 0.05$ A
Potential difference across R = $25 - 10 = 15$V
$15 = IR \Rightarrow R = \frac{15}{I} = \frac{15}{0.05} = 300\ \Omega$

questions.stem:
A gun mounted on the ground fires bullets in all directions with same speed. The farthest distance the bullets could reach is 6.4 m . The speed of the bullets from the gun is _______ m/s.
(take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution: $R_{max} = \frac{u^{2}}{g} = 6.4 \Rightarrow u = \sqrt{6.4 \times 10} = 8\ \mathrm{m/s}$

questions.stem:
Two identical small bar magnets each of dipole moment $3\sqrt{5}\ \mathrm{J/T}$ are placed at a center to center separation of 10 cm , with their axes perpendicular to each other as shown in figure. The value of magnetic field at the point P midway between the magnets is $\alpha \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______ .
$(\mu_{0} = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \mathrm{Tm/A})$
questions.solution:
(Figure: at P, $B_{1}$ along the line joining the magnets and $B_{2}$ perpendicular to it)
$B = \sqrt{B_{1}^{2} + B_{2}^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \sqrt{5}\,\frac{\mu_{0}}{4\pi} \cdot \frac{M}{r^{3}}$
$\Rightarrow 12 \times 10^{-3} \quad \therefore \alpha = 12$

questions.stem:
A circular coil of radius 2 cm and 125 turns carries a current of 1 A . The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.4 T . The axis of the coil makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the direction of the magnetic field. The torque acting on the coil is $\alpha \times 10^{-4}$ N.m. The value of $\alpha$ is ________ .
$(\pi = 3.14)$
questions.solution:
$\tau = MB\sin\theta = NiA.B.\sin\theta$
$= 125 \times 1 \times \pi(0.02)^{2} \times 0.4 \times \sin 30^\circ$
$= 314 \times 10^{-4}$

questions.stem: In a double slit experiment, when one of the slits is covered by a transparent mica sheet of refractive index 1.56 , the central fringe shifts to the position of $7^{th}$ bright fringe, obtained with both slits uncovered. If the light source wavelength is 450 nm , the thickness of mica sheet is $\alpha \times 10^{-9}$ m . The value of $\alpha$ is _______ .
questions.solution:
$7 \times \frac{D\lambda}{d} = \frac{D}{d}(\mu - 1)t$
$\Rightarrow t = \frac{7\lambda}{\mu - 1} = 5625 \times 10^{-9}$ m
